title: Residency fallback storyboard and customer scripting
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook and set of scripted vignettes to exercise region pin fallback behavior and the customer-facing messages that SRE/CS/AMs might need to send during degraded residency enforcement. Aim is to capture: what the operator does, what telemetry to gather (evidence), what the customer sees, and pre-baked wording for comms.

Scope / constraints:
- Focused on hosted + dedicated tenants that have an active region pin (hard or soft). Private deployments have separate runbooks but may use the same scripts for comms.
- Not a full incident postmortem template — this is an operational playtest and comms draft set.
- Assume key tooling available: residency-audit service, routing-proxy logs, region-assertion traces, request-level evidence capture (S3 bundle), and ticketing (JIRA).

Quick background (one-liner):
When a region pin is active, requests should be routed only to capacity in the pinned region. Fallback modes exist to (a) allow soft-fallthrough to allowed adjacent regions, (b) degrade to a compatible model variant in another region, or (c) fail closed. This doc tests user-impact for those modes and scripts operator steps.

Playtest vignettes (high level):
1) Transient infra hole in pinned region (zone-level power event) — soft-fallback allowed
   - Operator goals: keep service available, capture evidence proving we honored pin until forced fallback, document duration and percent of requests that hit fallback.
   - Steps: toggle simulated zone failure in staging; validate proxy fallback policy; sample 200 requests from flagged tenants; export routing-evidence bundle; run chargeback simulation.
   - Customer impact: <2s tail latency increase + 0.3% change in deterministic outputs for model-variant swap.
   - Customer script (short): "We observed a short disruption in your configured region. Traffic was automatically routed to a compatible fallback region to preserve availability. We collected routing evidence and will attach it to the incident ticket. No customer data was altered; latency may be slightly higher for ~15min."

2) Enforcement mismatch: tenant metadata asserts EU pin but control plane had stale anchor mapping — hard-pinning expected but some requests left region
   - Operator goals: identify extent of leakage, roll forward corrected mapping, surface artifact to legal for audit, notify customer with evidence.
   - Steps: run tenant-region-reconciliation job, pull audit log for period X, compute list of deliveries outside pin, coordinate with legal to confirm whether retention obligations were violated.
   - Evidence artifact: CSV of request ids + timestamps + destination region + policy-version.
   - Customer script (detailed): "We detected a mapping mismatch that permitted a small subset of requests to route outside your configured region between 02:17–02:51 UTC. We understand residency commitments are important; we’ve attached a request-by-request export and initiated a retention check. Next steps: (1) we will revoke offending logs per your preference, (2) we’ll propose tighter verification gates during pin updates, and (3) we’ll offer a compliance sync with your security lead."

3) Capacity shortage with automatic model-variant fallback (latency-sensitive customers)
   - Operator goals: choose fallback that matches customer SLAs; measure inference-quality delta; ensure customer is offered rollback.
   - Steps: enable canary variant in fallback region, sample model outputs against golden prompts, compute BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim similarity scores, report below-threshold cases.
   - Customer script (brief): "To avoid service interruption we served a compatible model variant hosted in a neighboring region. We validated output quality on representative samples; some prompts may show small differences. If you require strict bit-for-bit parity we can pause fallbacks and prefer a short outage window while we scale capacity."

Operator checklist (quick actionable):
- Immediately: tag incident with residency:affected-tenant and pin-mode in JIRA, start evidence capture job (residency-evidence/collect.sh).
- Within 10m: run inventory script to list capacity pools and active pins (residency-inventory --since 1h).
- Evidence to collect: routing-proxy logs, region-assertion headers, control-plane pin-change events, model-variant selection logs, tenant-declaration snapshot.
- Safety: if >1% of a tenant's requests left pinned region during a hard pin window, escalate to legal@redwood and add retention-eviction tag.

Evidence bundle format (proposed minimal fields):
- request_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id, route_decision, destination_region, policy_version, control_plane_event_id
- store as CSV and gzip; attach S3 link to ticket.

Sample operator CLI snippets (notes to self):
- Collect recent cross-region deliveries: 
  residency-audit export --tenant $TENANT --from 2025-02-10T00:00Z --to 2025-02-10T03:00Z --out /tmp/$TENANT-evidence.csv
- Re-run reconciliation: 
  residency-control reconcile-mapping --tenant $TENANT --dry-run | tee /tmp/reconcile-run.log

Customer notification templates (two lengths):
- Short alert (severity=info): 
  Subject: Short disruption routed to fallback region
  Body: "We experienced an infrastructure disruption in your pinned region and routed traffic to a compatible region to preserve availability. We captured evidence (attached) and expect service to be fully normal within 30 minutes. Contact your AM for more details."

- Expanded notice (severity=action): 
  Subject: Residency routing mismatch detected — evidence attached
  Body: "We found your tenant’s region mapping was inconsistent and a subset of requests were routed outside your pinned region between <start> and <end>. We have attached a per-request export and next steps we are taking (revoke logs, tighten validation gates, post-incident review). If you want immediate remediation options or to schedule a compliance call, reply and we’ll prioritize."

Telemetry signals to monitor (for automated alerting):
- percent_requests_outside_pin_per_tenant (5m/1h windows)
- avg_latency_delta_fallback_vs_pin (p95)
- model_variant_switch_rate_by_tenant
- control_plane_pin_update_rate + pin_update_error_rate

Risk-acceptance heuristics (brainstorm):
- Soft-fallback allowed for <0.5% of requests in a sliding 1h window for non-regulated tiers.
- For enterprise (>contracted_sla) customers, default to fail-closed unless customer has explicitly opted into fallback in contract.
- Any leakage >0.1% for hard-pinned tenants triggers legal notification.

Open questions / unresolved items (TODOs):
- How do we cryptographically sign evidence bundles so customers can independently verify chain-of-custody? (ask infra-crypto)
- Should we auto-redact prompt text from evidence bundles by default for regs that require minimization? (privacy/legal)
- Where to persist pin-version history for 7+ years for audit—S3 with locking or dedicated ledger?
- What exact SLA language do we need in contracts to allow soft fallbacks during catastrophic events? (sales/legal)

Suggested immediate next steps for a playtest run (owner: Hannah):
1) Schedule a 2-hour zone-failure playtest with SRE + solutions engineering (pickup date: Feb week 3).
2) Create a small set of 10 golden prompts and tenant test-seed to measure variant drift.
3) Prototype signed evidence bundle (minimal PoC) and attach to a follow-up doc for legal review.

Notes to reviewer (informal):
- This is intentionally sketchy — want to keep scripts short so on-call can copy/paste.
- Prefer a day where product/security can join the tabletop so contract implications are discussed in real time.
- If adopted, we should translate the short/expanded customer scripts into canned Slack + email templates under cs-templates repo.

Appendix: quick glossary
- hard pin: tenant must be served only from declared region(s); enforcement strict, fail-closed policy.
- soft fallback: allow routing to approved neighboring regions to maintain uptime; generally used for non-regulated workloads.
- evidence bundle: per-request export used to prove routing decisions during a time window.

End of doc.

(Notes: iterative doc. will add sample CSV schema and simple Python helper next pass.)
